- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer below forecast or adjust downward early.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply decay factor or cap forecast at +5% above peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting downward; delay forecast drop by 1–2 days or apply smoothing filter.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day moving average or dampen trend sensitivity.
